txt: His companion can barely suppress a yawn.
His companion leans forward, ready to jump in...
His companion nods his head with expectation.
His companion nods in agreement.
His companion nods, but offers no further solace.
His companion's eyes widen as you hold up the ancient weapon.
His companion's eyes widen with interest. He has a cold smile.
His friend yawns, evidently bored by literal reality.
His friend, though, seems oddly unmoved.
The young man's companion reflexively snorts at the mention of Gottwaldians and Econoclards.
The young man's companion says nothing, but the expression on his face reveals a begrudging respect for your experimental approach to character creation.
"'Those committed to the rights of property are those most apt to violate them'." His companion nods emphatically.
"'To find victory in the cultural war we must first scout the battlefield'."
"... something of an ideological auxiliary, perhaps."
"A gang of cheap psychologists and intellectual midgets." His companion sneers. "Typical Gottwalders, in other words."
"Abelard's 'Un Pays Infernal'..."
"Alright. You go next, Steban."
"And before that, there was Abelard's 'Un Pays Infernal'..."
"And of course, we'll be shooting right back."
"Another coffee, Steban?"
"As long as we maintain the appropriate critical distance."
"Basically indistinguishable from fascists. You'd need an x-ray machine to tell the difference."
"Besides, it would look pretty bad if people thought we were collaborating with the gendarmerie."
"But she refuses to submit an essay, so we can't call her a member of the group *per se*."
"But that would imply that whenever you unpeel time you leave behind some kind of *doppelgänger* in now-time..."
"Can't let any of the dreck rub off on you."
"Completely counter to the spirit of 'Wirrâl'. What's even the point?"
"Completely right, Steban."
"Comrade Steban is a great discussion leader. One of the best at the university."
"Damn it to hell!"
"Don't forget about Maurice and the turnips."
"Don't worry, I'm sure your jacket will turn up."
"Drip after drip after drip after drip..." The young man's companion appears to be mashing his fist into his palm.
"Eight cups a day is perfectly healthy."
"Exactly what I've been saying. On fundamental matters there can be no compromise!"
"Ha! As though you can call that pablum *teaching*."
"Harder to believe, but still possible..."
"He just quit coming. We haven't seen him around for weeks."
"He looks like he's about to puke."
"He probably won't get a better chance, honestly."
"He says he doesn't have any questions, Steban."
"He should know the meeting starts at 22.00 *sharp*." His companion looks up at you and squints.
"He wants to know if women are bourgeois, Steban..."
"He'll shit himself! Positively."
"Hey, Steban. Isn't that *your* jacket?"
"Hmm. I thought the *cloak-and-dagger routine* made us seem more appealing."
"Hmm. Then what does that make the *game designers*?"
"Hmmm, I guess no one could accuse Cindy of having a *bourgeois aesthetic*."
"Hmmm, it *does* sound pretty cool when you describe it like that."
"Hmph. Leave it to the gendarme to enforce bourgeois stylistic values."
"I believe it's 'Man is the mirror of the world'."
"I bet he's never written a substantial essay himself. He's really got no right to critique. None at all."
"I can't believe someone just left these matchboxes here."
"I still like the hill dweorgr for their Master Ironworking feat."
"I suppose that makes it a historical inevitability, beyond contradiction."
"I suppose we have read through most of the infra-materialist canon by this point."
"I would commit war crimes for some real Saramirizian coffee."
"I'll spit in Maurice's face when he comes crawling back."
"If he wants a real critical history, he's got to read 'On the Material Conditions of the Mirovan Boilermakers'."

"If only! They've got all the beans accounted for in their asset sheets, their quarterly budgets, their future projections. But for some reason there are never enough beans to go around, so we've just got to cut our bean rations in half..."
"If you encountered it in a novel, you'd say it sounded like a plot contrivance, or like a fantasy."
"In 'Innocence of Capital', Puncher and Wattmann argue that communists must possess as little capital as possible, in order to keep their thinking *undiluted* by its influence..."
"It appears so."
"It doesn't have to be a *hard* hit." He indicates his cheek. "Just enough to leave a mark."
"It doesn't sound like he's done the reading, Steban."
"It happens to the best of us."
"It is, it is..."
"It is, it's holding!"
"It means you're not a communist, in other words."
"It seems the face of violent reaction has revealed itself..."
"It was just a little *informal* experiment. No reason to take it too seriously."
"It was unbelievable. He said, 'Turnips don't care if they're grown by communists, moralists, or welkin. They grow just the same'."
"It will turn up, I'm sure. In a way, it wants to be found..."
"It's a sad reflection on our educational institutions."
"It's alright, Steban. That was still *very* close. One of our best performances yet."
"It's holding, it's holding..."
"It's my fault, Steban. My hands were shaking... Nerves got the better of me."
"It's too bad she hasn't developed the theoretical foundation to do truly radical work."
"Makes you want to gouge your eyes out. Or better, gouge the author's eyes out."
"Maybe he can explain himself."
"Mazov says it's the arrogance of capital that will be its ultimate undoing. It does not believe it can fail, which is why it must fail."
"Mazov tells us to laugh at the monster that hides behind false hopes and pieties."
"Not as good as Steban's original idea, though."
"Obviously." He snorts.
"Only because certain moralists and their ideological lap dogs pretend to object to his more *maximalist* tactics... as though they've never committed any so-called 'war crimes'."
"Or even *third*."
"Perhaps he subscribes to 'La Fumée'."
"Precisely my point. It's about quality, not quantity."
"Precisely. It's only beneath the cold light of scorn that deep truths are revealed..."
"Precisely. We're not interested in senseless parroting. We like to read *critically*."
"Providing you haven't been hanging out with non-communists, like Maurice."
"Really just violence in general. I find it *fascinating*."
"See, Steban? I told you there's no such thing as a gendarme communist."
"See? Even a gendarme gets it."
"See? Even the gendarme agrees."
"Seems unlikely, from a strictly infra-materialist perspective..."
"She said if she's going to make truly radical art, she needs a suitably radical workspace."
"Sleep well, gendarme."
"Some of our former comrades didn't have the *ideological fortitude* our work demands."
"Steban's right. If it's going to happen, it will happen."
"Steban's welkin is so mega. He's got this umbral stave that gives him *ungodly* bonuses against shadowborn."
"Steban, a moment..." The young man's companion beckons him into a private conference.
"Steban, can you hear me?"
"Steban, it's getting pretty late."
"Steban, you can't be serious... for a gendarme?"
"Steban? Are you alright?"
"Strange. I thought that women were attracted to a certain amount of revolutionary musk..."
"Thank god we're no Gottwaldians."
"That I did not expect." His companion is blushing now, a sheepish grin on his face.
"That means go home, gendarme."
"That was remarkable."
"That's interesting. I thought people *loved* group interviews."
"That's really good, Steban. You should save that for an essay."
"The communards didn't commit *enough* atrocities."
"The idea," his companion jumps in, "is to show Maurice and those other traitors that we're the only reading group *hard core* enough to tangle with the RCM..."
"The irradiated waste tokens have this great metallic ochre sheen."
"This gendarme talks just like a moralist. They *love* getting on their high horses about so-called 'war crimes'."
"This new translation of 'Reál and Reality' is garbage."
"Though *some of us* maintain that advertising is an unacceptably bourgeois tactic."
"Though historically speaking, the SRV *has supported* direct action against right-wing paramilitary squads, especially when they're doing the Indotribes' dirty work."
"Truly extraordinary."
"Undoubtedly."
"University is a lot better once you stop going to class."
"Wait, Steban, are you saying the gendarme is some kind of *future communist*?"
"We prefer difficult books. Books that might destroy you, if you don't destroy them first."
"We should probably clean up..."
"We think of ourselves as more of an intellectual vanguard."
"We're post-attendance, basically."
"We've tried it ourselves, but thus far we haven't been able to absorb more than the preface and table of contents."
"What does it say, Steban? I can't see."
"When nothing could be further from the truth."
"With his 'partner', he says."
"Yes, I would say he's got serious potential at least."
"Yes, a fascinating case study..."
"Yes, exactly."
"Yes, that's probably the best way to describe it."
"Yes, this worked out quite nicely." He seems immensely pleased with himself.
"Yes. One of our better discussions lately, on the whole."
"Yes. This is the closest we've ever gotten."
"Zuzanna said that he has been hanging out with some non-communists lately."
“He’s studying macro- *and* micro-economics.”
